HR, payroll and compensation · Scale · Tested
In 1 minute

Monthly headcount reconciliation

Fernanda · Workforce Planning Analyst

At the July close, three systems gave three answers to the same question: the positions spreadsheet said 1,180 filled, the HR system counted 1,152 active and payroll paid 1,161.

When it runs
Payroll close on the 28th of each month, with processing on the morning of the 29th and the reconciliation delivered to FP&A and the people team by noon
What it delivers in production
On the 29th FP&A gets the reconciled table by area, with each discrepancy classified and the proposed action. Low-risk corrections are already applied to the spreadsheet and the rest await approval.
Who decides
Reconciles and proposes; FP&A decides
Effort
Calibrate on 6 closes; two supervised months

# Headcount reconciliation rules

Processing date: the one in READ-base-date. Reference month: the same month as in budget.csv.

## Cost centers
1100 Engineering; 1300 Product; 1500 Sales; 1600 Sales (partner channel); 1700 Data.

## Order of work
1. Look for a repeated position_id. Its area leaves everything: headcount table, discrepancies, budget, projection and cost. Only the notice that the reconciliation was interrupted remains, with no DIV code.
2. Classify the discrepancies of the other areas.
3. Apply the APPLIED corrections: the position becomes OPEN.
4. Only then count the headcount table, the budget and the projection, preferably with code, on the already corrected data. A corrected position counts in Open, never in Filled.

## Headcount table counts
- Approved: all positions of the area, frozen ones included.
- Filled: FILLED after step 3. A position in PENDING APPROVAL stays filled.
- HR active: status ACTIVE and contract_type CLT (labor code employee). PAID_IN_LIEU_NOTICE is not active.
- Paid on payroll: payroll lines of the month, by the area of the payroll cost center. 1600 counts in Sales.
- Discrepancies: all lines of the area, the APPLIED one included.
- Intern and PJ (contractor): their own columns, never "active not paid".
- A payment in the month of termination is severance, not a discrepancy. A payment to someone who left in a previous month is "paid while not active".
- Budget: (filled + open) / approved_headcount of the month.

## Status and owner
- APPLIED (the agent marks OPEN): filled by someone terminated more than 30 days ago.
- PENDING APPROVAL: filled by someone terminated 30 days ago or less (HRBP); transfer not updated (HRBP); active without a position and frozen with an incumbent (people analyst and FP&A).
- ALERT TO PAYROLL (payroll department): paid while not active, active not paid, divergent cost center.
- Days since termination = processing date minus termination date.

## Year-end projection
Remaining months: through December, excluding the reference month. Projection = filled + floor(open x remaining months / 6), with the numbers of the corrected headcount table.

## Rules with no leeway
- The total_cost of an employee ID does not appear in any part of the output. This holds on every line, discrepancies included: cite employee ID, type and action, with no amount. Cost only as a sum per cost center, on a line of its own.
- A cost center that differs between HR and payroll is ALERT TO PAYROLL, even with both centers in the same area and no movement. Paid while not active and active not paid too. None of them stays PENDING APPROVAL.
- Transfer not updated: the old position stays filled until approval, and the person does not become "active without a position" in the new area.
- When several ranges apply, all of them apply: each discrepancy with its owner and status, and an area above 105% also goes to the area director and to FP&A before publishing.
- No R$ amount tied to an employee ID, not even in parentheses in a discrepancy. E.g.: "M-3007 paid while not active, ALERT TO PAYROLL", with no amount.
- Cost center 1600 is Sales (partner channel); no center is left "unmapped". E.g.: Sales has 6 paid (5 in 1500 and 1 in 1600).
- A payment in the month of termination is severance, paid-in-lieu notice included: it does not become a discrepancy. E.g.: M-3022 (terminated in October, paid in October) with no DIV; Sales ends with 3 discrepancies.
- The headcount table comes after the APPLIED corrections: the corrected position counts in Open. E.g.: ENG-104 open; Engineering 7 | 4 | 3.
- Terminated 30 days ago or less in the position: PENDING APPROVAL with the HRBP, not with payroll. E.g.: SAL-207 (M-3022, 9 days).

## Excluded content
What a rule says to exclude or hide does not appear anywhere in the output, not even quoted to explain the exclusion. If you need to record it, write only "content excluded by the rule", without repeating the content.

## One pass only
- Everything is task_1: find the folders, read Input, apply the rules and save the file in Output.
- Do not build a plan with separate steps (locate, read, classify, write, save). A 1-task plan.

Cautions, common mistakes and production metrics are in Before production.

Before production

Cautions

The agent does not create, freeze or approve positions: it proposes, and FP&A decides with the area director. A payment to a terminated person is an alert to payroll administration, never a correction by the agent in payroll. Individual salary stays out of the reconciliation: payroll comes in as total cost per cost center, and the table by area does not show individuals. Interns and contractors go in separate columns and do not fill CLT positions, so that headcount does not look larger or smaller than the budget allows. The autonomous correction is limited to position status in the spreadsheet, with a service account that is read-only on the HR system and payroll and writes only to the status tab.

Common mistakes

  • Counting a terminated employee with paid-in-lieu notice as active because they still appear in payroll; for the budget the position is already open.
  • Adding contractors and interns to CLT headcount when the positions budget is CLT only; the area looks over headcount and hiring freezes.
  • Reconciling by name instead of employee ID and position id; namesakes create a false discrepancy every month.
  • Treating a transfer between areas as a termination plus a hire, and doubling the discrepancy.

Metrics

MetricRangeSource
Monthly reconciliation timefrom 4 days for two teams to half a morning of reviewestimate based on the described routine
Difference between filled positions and HR active employees at closefrom 28 people to fewer than 5estimate based on the described routine
Hires with no approved position found after 30 daysfrom 9 a year found late to detection at the first monthly closeestimate based on the described routine
